claims.text: Adding 1 wt% Y2O3 to a FeCoNi-based high-entropy-alloy bond coat will improve coating durability and reliability relative to an undoped bond coat.
Adding Y2O3 to the feedstock during deposition can produce a uniform oxide dispersion in the bond coat.
Y2O3 addition will refine the bond-coat microstructure and produce smaller grains.
The added oxide particles will be dispersed at grain boundaries and within the FeCoNi-based matrix.
Y2O3 nanoparticles act as an oxygen scavenger in the bond coat.
Y2O3 nanoparticles act as a grain refiner in the bond coat.
The Y2O3 dispersion retards oxidation during high-temperature service.
The Y2O3 dispersion limits grain growth during high-temperature service.
Retarded oxidation and limited grain growth reduce bond-coat porosity.
Retarded oxidation and limited grain growth reduce phase instability during high-temperature service.
The proposed microstructural effects enhance interfacial bonding.
The proposed microstructural effects improve mechanical properties under extreme conditions.
The Y2O3-doped bond coat will have greater oxidation resistance than the untreated bond coat.
The Y2O3-doped bond coat will have greater cyclic durability than the untreated bond coat.
The Y2O3-doped bond coat will exhibit less microstructural degradation and defect formation during high-temperature service.
The improvement will remain effective above approximately 1200 °C and during repeated thermal cycling.
The magnitude of the improvement depends on oxide-dispersion homogeneity and processing parameters.
Prior evidence suggests that a 1 wt% Y2O3 oxide dispersion can improve oxidation resistance and grain structure.
